narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

cashier.instruct: Cheerful, slightly bored store cashier, bright and friendly.

boss.instruct: Confident, polished company executive on a TV interview, smooth and pleased with himself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You just bought a brand new printer for forty-nine dollars. What a steal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It prints concert tickets, homework, and a giant poster of your cat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twelve days later, a little red low ink light starts blinking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No problem. You drive to the store and grab two new cartridges.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ink costs more than the whole printer did.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That cheap printer was never the product. It was the bait.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Even the cheapest ink runs about thirteen dollars an ounce.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ounce for ounce, that's pricier than fine champagne.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And every cartridge hides a tiny chip that talks to the printer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One update in twenty sixteen made printers reject cheaper cartridges overnight.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then there's cleaning. Printers spray ink just to keep the heads from drying.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Testers found some burned half the ink or more without printing anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a few, only twenty to thirty percent ever reached the paper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One printer boss even said it on live TV.

lines.speaker: boss
lines.text: Every time a customer buys a printer, it's an investment for us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So you're not really the customer. You're the investment.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Back home, the brand new cartridge is already blinking.
